page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge is a KVM-hypervised virtual machine belonging to the ecs.gn6i family. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, supporting hyper-threading. It includes 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB per core. The hardware profile is distinguished by a bundled NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, providing 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance asymmetry. The host CPU and memory subsystem exhibit lower-tier performance, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU scores falling into the bottom 25% or bottom 10% categories. Memory read-only bandwidth for large uncached blocks is measured at 20.81 GB/sec, which is categorized as poor. Conversely, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong performance for specialized workloads. Large Language Model (LLM) inference benchmarks show top-tier results for prompt processing, reaching 8480.06 tokens/sec on a small 135M model and 1167.65 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are also strong, achieving 263.82 tokens/sec and 34.5 tokens/sec for the small and medium models respectively.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents an entry-level GPU-accelerated option where resource density is optimized for low-intensity parallel computing rather than heavy general-purpose CPU tasks. The tradeoff involves accepting lower CPU and memory throughput to gain cost-effective access to hardware-accelerated machine learning capabilities. Consequently, the ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge is suited for lightweight GPU-accelerated workloads such as small-to-medium scale LLM inference, basic machine learning model deployment, and entry-level graphics rendering, while being less suitable for CPU-bound applications, high-throughput database operations, or memory-intensive tasks.
